rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

human.problem: The question "What do they promise him?" never says who "they" are, and cards 14 and 15 also rely on an unnamed "they." The choice-card rule asks for that context. But Joshua 1:16 only says "they answered Joshua," so it leaves open whether the speakers are the two and a half eastern tribes or all the people. Filling in either one would break the leave-open rule.
human.question: When a choice card has to say who is speaking, but the text leaves the speaker open (Joshua 1:16), should the card name the group the context suggests (the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh)? Or should it use a neutral phrase like "the people answering Joshua," or something else?
